key_insight: An integrated deep learning and adaptive control method aims to help GMAW robots adjust welding parameters as joint geometry and seam conditions change.
engineering_relevance: Adaptive welding could reduce manual reprogramming and help maintain weld quality despite assembly deviations and heat-induced changes.
method: Quality-grade-oriented planning with site-specific multi-objective parameter optimization.
Semi-supervised seam and molten-pool segmentation, plus neural-network weld-formation prediction for spatter suppression.
Fuzzy adaptive control to adjust the welding process.
evidence_signal: Experiments used Q235 steel butt joints and developed a response surface model relating current, welding speed, torch angle and nozzle height to weld geometry; the abstract reports no quantitative performance gains.
watch_item: Generalization beyond Q235 steel butt joints and robustness under production conditions require further validation.
paper_title: Deep Learning-Based Welding Process Optimization and Adaptive Control Method for Welding Robots
